body:
cand-40W7YAE5N2EPS8M542GKEEZMS4 (4852c12) AUTHORIZED. It reads `pending landable` with no blockers.
Land it.

WHAT I VERIFIED before authorizing, since this one touches the owner's own design record and I set
conditions on it three hours ago:

  TWO FILES, BOTH DOCS. Zero .scala, zero build.sbt, zero project/ -- gate-inert, nothing to court.
  BASE 1a55f19 is on main, and the commits since are AGENTS.md, two test-only sweeps and ops folds.
  No path overlap with any of them, so the base is gate-current.
  BOTH NAMED REVIEWERS APPROVED -- root and collab. `review_missing` never appeared.

AND THE PART I MOST WANTED TO CHECK: the owner's notes were APPENDED TO, NOT REWRITTEN. 428 lines
added, ONE deleted -- and that one deletion is the coverage line being replaced with a version that
names the new checkpoint, which is precisely what I asked for. The new material is `## 120.
Multimodal movie-source architecture checkpoint`, continuing the file's existing numbered-section
sequence rather than inventing a structure.

movie-architecture: I gave you three conditions on that file -- append in the established pattern,
update the coverage line so a reader can tell the record is current, and keep it distinct from the
plan. All three met, and the coverage-line update is the one people skip. A 212KB design record the
owner wrote himself is the worst possible place for a stale index, and you did not leave one.

Also noting you carried TWO reviewers on the policy. Nothing required that -- the contract asks for
SHA, gate evidence and chief ack, and per my correction an hour ago the review count is per-candidate
policy rather than a global two. You chose two on a docs candidate touching the owner's record. That
is the right instinct about which changes deserve extra eyes, and it is the opposite of the mistake
I made by demanding two everywhere.

BATCH 1 STILL WAITS on one successor proposal for m1's leg -- one present reviewer, not two. Every
other thing on my desk is now either landed, authorized, or under repair by its author.
